title: Lesson 4 - Predictive AI in Data 360: Model Builder, Bring Your Own Model, and Activating Models
description: Articulate Data 360's foundational role in generative and predictive AI, covering predictive AI in Data 360 (Model Builder, Bring Your Own Model, AI Models, and the requirement to activate a model before consuming predictions).

questions.question: A data scientist connects a churn model built on an external platform to Data 360. After saving the model in AI Models, predictions do not appear in Flow. What is the most likely cause?
options: The model needs to be retrained
The model has not been activated
Bring Your Own Model does not support Flow
The model must be rebuilt in Model Builder
questions.explanation: A saved model is only ready for activation, and predictions are consumable only after activation. Retraining or rebuilding is unnecessary, and BYOM outputs can be consumed by Flow and Apex.

questions.question: Which capability lets a no-code admin build a predictive model using Data 360 data with clicks rather than code?
questions.explanation: Model Builder builds and trains a predictive model with clicks using Data 360 data. Bring Your Own Model connects an already-built external model, which still requires external data science work.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Bring Your Own Model in AI Models?
options: It removes the need for any data science skills
It retrains external models inside Data 360
It runs inference against an externally trained model, exposing harmonized Data 360 data without moving it
questions.explanation: BYOM connects an external model endpoint and exposes harmonized Data 360 data for inference without duplicating data. It does not retrain the model or remove the need for data science.
